question: Not shared at the level of population class. Both papers detect current (cross-sectional) MCI against non-MCI from clinical and questionnaire tabular data in Chinese hospital patients, so the task, comparison and channel match (the record's 'P-307 = retinal' is wrong; P-307 uses no imaging). The populations behind the label are two different disease-defined groups, and neither is a subset of the other. P-343 studies hospitalised type 2 diabetes patients aged 40 or over in an endocrinology department (Nanjing Drum Tower Hospital), and the authors say the model is mainly applicable to older patients with poorer glycaemic control. P-307 studies patients aged 60 or over with chronic pain in a pain department (Nanchang; mean age 71.1). The predictors are tied to each population's defining condition and share only age and education: eGFR, systolic blood pressure, BMI, diabetes duration and a glucolipid index in P-343; pain level, pain sites, pain duration, depression and sleep in P-307. Both use MoCA < 26 inside a clinical MCI definition (AAN 2018 in P-343; Petersen/IWG with neurologist confirmation in P-307). P-307's authors treat MCI identification in chronic-pain patients as a question distinct from the one answered by existing models for diabetic patients.

figures.P-343: Internal (Table 2, tuned SVC): 0.74 +/- 0.04 (CV mean and SD; the extract prints '0 74 ± 0 04'). Mean +/- 1.96 SD: [0.662, 0.818]. Hanley-McNeil at the 623-person validation split (about 218 MCI/405 NC): Q1 = 0.5873, Q2 = 0.6294, SE = 0.0218, [0.697, 0.783]. Other internal models: LR 0.73 +/- 0.01, AdaBoost (tuned) 0.76 +/- 0.01, CatBoost (tuned) 0.73 +/- 0.02. External DECODE (Table 3 SVC row; abstract): 0.80, no interval; n = 161 (Figure 1: 189 minus 20 illiterate minus 8 with insufficient data); class split derived from the printed accuracy 0.75, recall 0.89 and precision 0.72: P = 161*0.25/(0.11 + 0.89*0.3889) = 40.25/0.4561 = 88.2, so about 88 MCI/73 NC. Hanley-McNeil: Q1 = 0.6667, Q2 = 0.7111, SE^2 = 7.600/6424, SE = 0.0344, CI [0.733, 0.867] ([0.712, 0.888] even at a skewed 40/121 split).
figures.P-307: Testing set (30%, n = 184; about 51 MCI/133 non-MCI at 27.6%), 95% CIs as printed (Table 2): XGBoost 0.925 [0.863, 0.995]; LR 0.895 [0.829, 0.966]; AdaBoost 0.868 [0.770, 0.972]; SVM 0.757 [0.672, 0.844]. A Hanley-McNeil check for XGBoost at 51/133 gives SE = 0.0264, [0.873, 0.977]; the printed, wider interval is used.

matched_figure_check: No figure is reported in the other's population or with the other's predictors, so nothing removes the population difference. On the matched validation stage (internal random splits), P-343's 0.74 (at most [0.662, 0.818]) and P-307's 0.925 [0.863, 0.995] have non-overlapping intervals. The recorded pairing (P-343 external 0.80 [0.733, 0.867] against 0.925) differs both ways: each estimate lies outside the other's interval, though the intervals touch between 0.863 and 0.867. By model family the picture is mixed: P-307's SVM 0.757 [0.672, 0.844] agrees with P-343's SVC 0.74; P-307's LR 0.895 [0.829, 0.966] differs from P-343's LR 0.73; P-307's AdaBoost 0.868 [0.770, 0.972] narrowly excludes P-343's tuned AdaBoost 0.76. Architecture is an allowed difference, not a matched condition, and at the matched validation stage the gap persists. No matched figure reconciles the pair.
performance_validity: Section 3.5 exclusion not met: P-307's 0.925 is below 0.97 (n = 612, internal split only), and P-343 has 2074 participants plus an external cohort. A caution for any use of P-307's figure: its test-set precision (0.882) equals its specificity (0.882), which holds only at 1:1 class balance; at the test set's expected 27.6% prevalence the same sensitivity and specificity would give precision of about 0.74. The reported test metrics therefore appear to have been computed on class-balanced data (SMOTETomek resampling or the 10-fold CV the methods mention), so 0.925 may be optimistic.
reason: The AUCs differ beyond uncertainty on the recorded figures (0.80 [0.733, 0.867] against 0.925 [0.863, 0.995]) and at the matched internal stage (0.74 against 0.925), and no matched figure reconciles them. But they describe MCI detection in two different disease-defined populations (hospitalised adults with type 2 diabetes against older chronic-pain patients) with predictors specific to each condition, so the pair fails condition 1, as C-183 does. If the operator read 'Chinese hospital patients with a clinical MCI diagnosis' as one class, conditions 2 to 6 would hold, with population, predictors, validation tier and P-307's apparently balanced evaluation as the candidate explanations.
